gov-a.01.statement: What is the form of government of the United States? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Republic | Constitution-based federal republic | Representative democracy | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government

gov-a.02.statement: What is the supreme law of the land? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: (U.S.) Constitution | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government

gov-a.03.statement: Name one thing the U.S. Constitution does. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Forms the government | Defines powers of government | Defines the parts of government | Protects the rights of the people | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government
answers: Protects the rights of the people

gov-a.04.statement: The U.S. Constitution starts with the words "We the People." What does "We the People" mean? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Self-government | Popular sovereignty | Consent of the governed | People should govern themselves | (Example of) social contract | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government

gov-a.05.statement: How are changes made to the U.S. Constitution? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Amendments | The amendment process | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government

gov-a.06.statement: What does the Bill of Rights protect? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: (The basic) rights of Americans | (The basic) rights of people living in the United States | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government
answers: (The basic) rights of people living in the United States

gov-a.07.statement: How many amendments does the U.S. Constitution have? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Twenty-seven (27) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government

gov-a.08.statement: Why is the Declaration of Independence important? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: It says America is free from British control. | It says all people are created equal. | It identifies inherent rights. | It identifies individual freedoms. | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government
answers: It says America is free from British control.
It says all people are created equal.

gov-a.09.statement: What founding document said the American colonies were free from Britain? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Declaration of Independence | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government

gov-a.10.statement: Name two important ideas from the Declaration of Independence and the U.S. Constitution. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Equality | Liberty | Social contract | Natural rights | Limited government | Self-government | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government

gov-a.11.statement: The words "Life, Liberty, and the pursuit of Happiness" are in what founding document? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Declaration of Independence | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government

gov-a.12.statement: What is the economic system of the United States? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Capitalism | Free market economy | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government

gov-a.13.statement: What is the rule of law? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Everyone must follow the law. | Leaders must obey the law. | Government must obey the law. | No one is above the law. | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government
answers: No one is above the law.

gov-a.14.statement: Many documents influenced the U.S. Constitution. Name one. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Declaration of Independence | Articles of Confederation | Federalist Papers | Anti-Federalist Papers | Virginia Declaration of Rights | Fundamental Orders of Connecticut | Mayflower Compact | Iroquois Great Law of Peace | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government

gov-a.15.statement: There are three branches of government. Why? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: So one part does not become too powerful | Checks and balances | Separation of powers | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — A: Principles of American Government
answers: So one part does not become too powerful

gov-b.01.statement: Name the three branches of government. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Legislative, executive, and judicial | Congress, president, and the courts | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.02.statement: The President of the United States is in charge of which branch of government? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Executive branch | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.03.statement: What part of the federal government writes laws? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: (U.S.) Congress | (U.S. or national) legislature | Legislative branch | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.04.statement: What are the two parts of the U.S. Congress? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Senate and House (of Representatives) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.05.statement: Name one power of the U.S. Congress. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Writes laws | Declares war | Makes the federal budget | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.06.statement: How many U.S. senators are there? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: One hundred (100) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.07.statement: How long is a term for a U.S. senator? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Six (6) years | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.08.statement: Who is one of your state's U.S. senators now? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Answers will vary. [District of Columbia residents and residents of U.S. territories should answer that D.C. (or the territory where the applicant lives) has no U.S. senators.] | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: Answers will vary. [District of Columbia residents and residents of U.S. territories should answer that D.C. (or the territory where the applicant lives) has no U.S. senators.]

gov-b.09.statement: How many voting members are in the House of Representatives? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Four hundred thirty-five (435) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.10.statement: How long is a term for a member of the House of Representatives? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Two (2) years | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.11.statement: Why do U.S. representatives serve shorter terms than U.S. senators? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: To more closely follow public opinion | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: To more closely follow public opinion

gov-b.12.statement: How many senators does each state have? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Two (2) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.13.statement: Why does each state have two senators? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Equal representation (for small states) | The Great Compromise (Connecticut Compromise) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.14.statement: Name your U.S. representative. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Answers will vary. [Residents of territories with nonvoting Delegates or Resident Commissioners may provide the name of that Delegate or Commissioner. Also acceptable is any statement that the territory has no (voting) representatives in Congress.] | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: Answers will vary. [Residents of territories with nonvoting Delegates or Resident Commissioners may provide the name of that Delegate or Commissioner. Also acceptable is any statement that the territory has no (voting) representatives in Congress.]

gov-b.15.statement: What is the name of the Speaker of the House of Representatives now? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Visit uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates for the name of the Speaker of the House of Representatives. | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: Visit uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates for the name of the Speaker of the House of Representatives.

gov-b.16.statement: Who does a U.S. senator represent? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Citizens of their state | People of their state | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.17.statement: Who elects U.S. senators? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Citizens from their state | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.18.statement: Who does a member of the House of Representatives represent? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Citizens in their (congressional) district | Citizens in their district | People from their (congressional) district | People in their district | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.19.statement: Who elects members of the House of Representatives? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Citizens from their (congressional) district | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.20.statement: Some states have more representatives than other states. Why? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: (Because of) the state's population | (Because) they have more people | (Because) some states have more people | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.21.statement: The President of the United States is elected for how many years? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Four (4) years | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.22.statement: The President of the United States can serve only two terms. Why? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: (Because of) the 22nd Amendment | To keep the president from becoming too powerful | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: To keep the president from becoming too powerful

gov-b.23.statement: What is the name of the President of the United States now? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Visit uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates for the name of the President of the United States. | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: Visit uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates for the name of the President of the United States.

gov-b.24.statement: What is the name of the Vice President of the United States now? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Visit uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates for the name of the Vice President of the United States. | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: Visit uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates for the name of the Vice President of the United States.

gov-b.25.statement: If the president can no longer serve, who becomes president? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: The Vice President (of the United States) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: The Vice President (of the United States)

gov-b.26.statement: Name one power of the president. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Signs bills into law | Vetoes bills | Enforces laws | Commander in Chief (of the military) | Chief diplomat | Appoints federal judges | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.27.statement: Who is Commander in Chief of the U.S. military? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: The President (of the United States) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.28.statement: Who signs bills to become laws? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: The President (of the United States) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.29.statement: Who vetoes bills? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: The President (of the United States) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.30.statement: Who appoints federal judges? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: The President (of the United States) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.31.statement: The executive branch has many parts. Name one. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: President (of the United States) | Cabinet | Federal departments and agencies | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.32.statement: What does the President's Cabinet do? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Advises the President (of the United States) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: Advises the President (of the United States)

gov-b.33.statement: What are two Cabinet-level positions? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Attorney General | Secretary of Agriculture | Secretary of Commerce | Secretary of Education | Secretary of Energy | Secretary of Health and Human Services | Secretary of Homeland Security | Secretary of Housing and Urban Development | Secretary of the Interior | Secretary of Labor | Secretary of State | Secretary of Transportation | Secretary of the Treasury | Secretary of Veterans Affairs | Secretary of War (Defense) | Vice-President | Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency | Administrator of the Small Business Administration | Director of the Central Intelligence Agency | Director of the Office of Management and Budget | Director of National Intelligence | United States Trade Representative | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: Secretary of Health and Human Services
Secretary of Housing and Urban Development
Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency
Administrator of the Small Business Administration
Director of the Central Intelligence Agency
Director of the Office of Management and Budget

gov-b.34.statement: Why is the Electoral College important? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: It decides who is elected president. | It provides a compromise between the popular election of the president and congressional selection. | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: It decides who is elected president.
It provides a compromise between the popular election of the president and congressional selection.

gov-b.35.statement: What is one part of the judicial branch? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Supreme Court | Federal Courts | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.36.statement: What does the judicial branch do? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Reviews laws | Explains laws | Resolves disputes (disagreements) about the law | Decides if a law goes against the (U.S.) Constitution | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: Decides if a law goes against the (U.S.) Constitution

gov-b.37.statement: What is the highest court in the United States? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Supreme Court | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.38.statement: How many seats are on the Supreme Court? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Nine (9) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.39.statement: How many Supreme Court justices are usually needed to decide a case? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Five (5) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.40.statement: How long do Supreme Court justices serve? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: (For) life | Lifetime appointment | (Until) retirement | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.41.statement: Supreme Court justices serve for life. Why? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: To be independent (of politics) | To limit outside (political) influence | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.42.statement: Who is the Chief Justice of the United States now? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Visit uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates for the name of the Chief Justice of the United States. | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: Visit uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates for the name of the Chief Justice of the United States.

gov-b.43.statement: Name one power that is only for the federal government. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Print paper money | Mint coins | Declare war | Create an army | Make treaties | Set foreign policy | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.44.statement: Name one power that is only for the states. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Provide schooling and education | Provide protection (police) | Provide safety (fire departments) | Give a driver's license | Approve zoning and land use | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government

gov-b.45.statement: What is the purpose of the 10th Amendment? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: (It states that the) powers not given to the federal government belong to the states or to the people. | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: (It states that the) powers not given to the federal government belong to the states or to the people.

gov-b.46.statement: Who is the governor of your state now? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Answers will vary. [District of Columbia residents should answer that D.C. does not have a governor.] | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: Answers will vary. [District of Columbia residents should answer that D.C. does not have a governor.]

gov-b.47.statement: What is the capital of your state? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Answers will vary. [District of Columbia residents should answer that D.C. is not a state and does not have a capital. Residents of U.S. territories should name the capital of the territory.] | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — B: System of Government
answers: Answers will vary. [District of Columbia residents should answer that D.C. is not a state and does not have a capital. Residents of U.S. territories should name the capital of the territory.]

gov-c.01.statement: There are four amendments to the U.S. Constitution about who can vote. Describe one of them. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Citizens eighteen (18) and older (can vote). | You don't have to pay (a poll tax) to vote. | Any citizen can vote. (Women and men can vote.) | A male citizen of any race (can vote). | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — C: Rights and Responsibilities
answers: You don't have to pay (a poll tax) to vote.
Any citizen can vote. (Women and men can vote.)
A male citizen of any race (can vote).

gov-c.02.statement: Who can vote in federal elections, run for federal office, and serve on a jury in the United States? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Citizens | Citizens of the United States | U.S. citizens | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — C: Rights and Responsibilities

gov-c.03.statement: What are three rights of everyone living in the United States? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Freedom of expression | Freedom of speech | Freedom of assembly | Freedom to petition the government | Freedom of religion | The right to bear arms | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — C: Rights and Responsibilities

gov-c.04.statement: What do we show loyalty to when we say the Pledge of Allegiance? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: The United States | The flag | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — C: Rights and Responsibilities

gov-c.05.statement: Name two promises that new citizens make in the Oath of Allegiance. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Give up loyalty to other countries | Defend the (U.S.) Constitution | Obey the laws of the United States | Serve in the military (if needed) | Serve (help, do important work for) the nation (if needed) | Be loyal to the United States | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — C: Rights and Responsibilities
answers: Give up loyalty to other countries
Obey the laws of the United States
Serve (help, do important work for) the nation (if needed)
Be loyal to the United States

gov-c.06.statement: How can people become United States citizens? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Be born in the United States, under the conditions set by the 14th Amendment | Naturalize | Derive citizenship (under conditions set by Congress) | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — C: Rights and Responsibilities
answers: Be born in the United States, under the conditions set by the 14th Amendment
Derive citizenship (under conditions set by Congress)

gov-c.07.statement: What are two examples of civic participation in the United States? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Vote | Run for office | Join a political party | Help with a campaign | Join a civic group | Join a community group | Give an elected official your opinion (on an issue) | Contact elected officials | Support or oppose an issue or policy | Write to a newspaper | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — C: Rights and Responsibilities
answers: Give an elected official your opinion (on an issue)
Support or oppose an issue or policy

gov-c.08.statement: What is one way Americans can serve their country? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Vote | Pay taxes | Obey the law | Serve in the military | Run for office | Work for local, state, or federal government | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — C: Rights and Responsibilities
answers: Work for local, state, or federal government

gov-c.09.statement: Why is it important to pay federal taxes? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Required by law | All people pay to fund the federal government | Required by the (U.S.) Constitution (16th Amendment) | Civic duty | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — C: Rights and Responsibilities
answers: All people pay to fund the federal government

gov-c.10.statement: It is important for all men age 18 through 25 to register for the Selective Service. Name one reason why. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Required by law | Civic duty | Makes the draft fair, if needed | domain: AMERICAN GOVERNMENT — C: Rights and Responsibilities
answers: Makes the draft fair, if needed

hist-a.05.statement: Name one reason why the Americans declared independence from Britain. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: High taxes | Taxation without representation | British soldiers stayed in Americans' houses (boarding, quartering) | They did not have self-government | Boston Massacre | Boston Tea Party (Tea Act) | Stamp Act | Sugar Act | Townshend Acts | Intolerable (Coercive) Acts | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — A: Colonial Period and Independence

hist-a.06.statement: Who wrote the Declaration of Independence? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: (Thomas) Jefferson | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — A: Colonial Period and Independence

hist-a.07.statement: When was the Declaration of Independence adopted? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: July 4, 1776 | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — A: Colonial Period and Independence

hist-a.08.statement: The American Revolution had many important events. Name one. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: (Battle of) Bunker Hill | Declaration of Independence | Washington Crossing the Delaware (Battle of Trenton) | (Battle of) Saratoga | Valley Forge (Encampment) | (Battle of) Yorktown (British surrender at Yorktown) | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — A: Colonial Period and Independence

hist-a.09.statement: There were 13 original states. Name five. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: New Hampshire | Massachusetts | Rhode Island | Connecticut | New York | New Jersey | Pennsylvania | Delaware | Maryland | Virginia | North Carolina | South Carolina | Georgia | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — A: Colonial Period and Independence

hist-a.10.statement: What founding document was written in 1787? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: (U.S.) Constitution | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — A: Colonial Period and Independence

hist-a.11.statement: The Federalist Papers supported the passage of the U.S. Constitution. Name one of the writers. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: (James) Madison | (Alexander) Hamilton | (John) Jay | Publius | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — A: Colonial Period and Independence

hist-a.12.statement: Why were the Federalist Papers important? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: They helped people understand the (U.S.) Constitution. | They supported passing the (U.S.) Constitution. | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — A: Colonial Period and Independence

hist-a.13.statement: Benjamin Franklin is famous for many things. Name one. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Founded the first free public libraries | First Postmaster General of the United States | Helped write the Declaration of Independence | Inventor | U.S. diplomat | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — A: Colonial Period and Independence

First Postmaster General of the United States
Helped write the Declaration of Independence

hist-a.14.statement: George Washington is famous for many things. Name one. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: "Father of Our Country" | First president of the United States | General of the Continental Army | President of the Constitutional Convention | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — A: Colonial Period and Independence

hist-a.15.statement: Thomas Jefferson is famous for many things. Name one. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Writer of the Declaration of Independence | Third president of the United States | Doubled the size of the United States (Louisiana Purchase) | First Secretary of State | Founded the University of Virginia | Writer of the Virginia Statute on Religious Freedom | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — A: Colonial Period and Independence
answers: Writer of the Declaration of Independence
Third president of the United States
Doubled the size of the United States (Louisiana Purchase)
Writer of the Virginia Statute on Religious Freedom

hist-a.16.statement: James Madison is famous for many things. Name one. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: "Father of the Constitution" | Fourth president of the United States | President during the War of 1812 | One of the writers of the Federalist Papers | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — A: Colonial Period and Independence

One of the writers of the Federalist Papers

hist-a.17.statement: Alexander Hamilton is famous for many things. Name one. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: First Secretary of the Treasury | One of the writers of the Federalist Papers | Helped establish the First Bank of the United States | Aide to General George Washington | Member of the Continental Congress | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — A: Colonial Period and Independence

Helped establish the First Bank of the United States

hist-b.01.statement: What territory did the United States buy from France in 1803? Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Louisiana Territory | Louisiana | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — B: 1800s

hist-b.02.statement: Name one war fought by the United States in the 1800s. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: War of 1812 | Mexican-American War | Civil War | Spanish-American War | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — B: 1800s

hist-b.03.statement: Name the U.S. war between the North and the South. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: The Civil War | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — B: 1800s

hist-b.04.statement: The Civil War had many important events. Name one. Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: (Battle of) Fort Sumter | Emancipation Proclamation | (Battle of) Vicksburg | (Battle of) Gettysburg | Sherman's March | (Surrender at) Appomattox | (Battle of) Antietam/Sharpsburg | Lincoln was assassinated. | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — B: 1800s

Acceptable answer(s) [M-1778 verbatim]: Freed the slaves (Emancipation Proclamation) | Saved (or preserved) the Union | Led the United States during the Civil War | 16th president of the United States | Delivered the Gettysburg Address | domain: AMERICAN HISTORY — B: 1800s
